title: An API term in other capitals saves and reads back in the term's spelling
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a valid Public API key for the test organization, the Public API documentation from the developers (it gives the request to create, update and read a customer), and a request tool.
  • Have the shop's own active term named "Net 10".
  • Choose a name for a new customer, customer A.
custom_steps:
1. Send a Public API request that creates customer A with the credit term "net 10".
  2. Send a Public API request that reads customer A.
  3. Open customer A's customer page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The request is accepted and customer A is created.

Step 2:

  • The credit term comes back as "Net 10" (the saved spelling).

Step 3:

  • The "Credit term" reads "Net 10".

The tester sends Public API requests in this case, using the Public API documentation: the engineering plan (26 Oct 2026) names the request that creates a customer POST /api/v1/customers; reading a customer back uses the read request the documentation gives.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 5 (26 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11679 (Story 10, Imports and Public API)

  • S10-R3: “A credit term that matches one of the shop's terms (standard or its own) ignoring capitals and spaces is saved in that term's spelling: "net 10", "NET10" and "Net 10" all save as the shop's "Net 10". This applies to customers and vendors created or updated by an import, and created or updated through the Public API.”
  • S10-R7: “The Public API reads, creates and updates a customer's credit term. It has no way to list the shop's terms or its default; an integrator sends a term name and reads back the saved spelling (S10-R3). The vendor API is unchanged except for one default: a vendor created through the Public API with no credit term starts on COD, as New Vendor does (S6-R2), instead of today’s unrecognized "net_30". Vendors created before release keep the term they have.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
